text: #929's steps 1 and 2, built by hand. A Go part's optional macos field in .invariant/repository.json declares build, vet and test, and named checks run after them in order, each a plain argument array: no shell, no {test} placeholder, no not_applicable reason in its place, no control character. Other languages can't declare it, since the job sets up Go alone, and omitted it stays out of the serialized contract, so execution digests don't change. The gate's second job, invariant/gate-macos, is an embedded fragment written after the invariant/gate job, because preflight reads the gate's job from gate.yml to its end. It runs on macos-26, GitHub's hosted macOS 26 image on Apple silicon (image 20261102.0473.1, macOS 26.7.2, Xcode 26.6 with the macOS 26.5 SDK when written), never macos-latest, which moves; macos-15 defaults to Xcode 16.4 and the macOS 15.5 SDK, and On Air builds and vets against the 26.5 SDK. The job builds the gate at the same pin, and checks with Go 1.27.1, toolchain.GoVersion, which a test ties to GoImage. invariant check-macos loads the contract at the base, stages the candidate as check-repository does without the projects directory, and runs every declared part's checks on every pull request and push, each whatever the one before did, with GOTOOLCHAIN=local and without any variable whose name holds TOKEN. It fails anywhere but macOS rather than skip, since a skipped required check counts as passed, and passes saying nothing was checked when the base declares no such part, as at the base of the pull request that adds one. check-repository says it didn't check such a part on macOS. init writes the job, and prints protection that requires both checks, only for a kept contract with such a part, and new declares none, so a repository without one gets the same files as before, which tests hold to digests taken before the change.
